title: Targeted rollback: Embed-v2 Canary — crib notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal crib for the targeted rollback of embed-v2 canary traffic. This is my scratchpad for the short morning standup and the Slack bulletin. Not polished — notes to self and things to confirm before we send any wider comms.

TL;DR:
- We are rolling the embed-v2 canary back to embed-v1 for 10% of traffic (canary slice) due to a subtle quality regression on short query prompts observed in the last 48h.
- Expected visible impact: small latency improvement (10–15ms) for canary, restored embedding similarity stability for critical customers.
- Action window: immediate (start), aim to complete within 30 minutes. Monitoring window: 60 minutes after rollback.

Audience for this note:
- On-call SRE and embed model owners (primary: eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml)
- Customer Success standby (for any inbound customer pings)
- Product PMs for hosted-embeddings (heads-up)

Objectives for the rollout/comm:
1) Reduce customer-exposed quality variance quickly while keeping scope tight.
2) Avoid alarm storm — keep messages factual and minimal.
3) Keep rollback reversible: preserve canary config as-is (we're changing routing only).

Key facts to surface in Slack announcement (short):
- What: temporary rollback of embed-v2 canary slice to embed-v1 for 10% traffic due to quality variance on short queries.
- When: starting now; expected < 30m for the change to take effect; we will monitor for 60m.
- Who: eng/ops on-call + model team. No customer-facing downtime expected.
- Ask: if you see customer reports or anomalous alerts, tag #ops-embed-incident and ping Priya.

Draft Slack bulletin (one-liner + details):
> Ops notice: rolling back embed-v2 canary (10% slice) to embed-v1 now due to observed short-query similarity regression. No downtime expected. Change should propagate in ~30m. Monitoring active for 60m. If you see customer impact, please message #ops-embed-incident and @Priya. JIRA: JIRA-5582.

Q&A (prep for quick replies):
Q: Will this affect production latency?
A: Slight improvement for the rollback slice (~10–15ms median). No other latency impact expected.

Q: Why rollback embed-v2 instead of fixing?
A: Regression is small but customer-visible on short prompts; we need immediate stability for a handful of paying customers. Embed-v2 fix is non-trivial (similarity calibration), needs a short PR + evals; rollback buys us time.

Q: Is any customer being notified?
A: Not proactively unless CS observes customer tickets or if the regression correlates with a specific account. CS standby: @Rowan.

Q: Is there risk of data loss or state mismatch?
A: No. This is stateless traffic routing — no data migration. KV/prefix caches unaffected.

Operational checklist (my running todo):
- [ ] Confirm runbook steps with Priya (done: 2025-11-04 08:12)
- [x] Open JIRA ticket JIRA-5582 (owner: Hiro)
- [x] Notify on-call in #ops-embed-incident (pinged at 08:18)
- [ ] Flip routing rule for canary slice from embed-v2 -> embed-v1 (platform console): initiate change and record request ID
- [ ] Verify traffic distribution in console and Datadog (canary slice shows embed-v1)
- [ ] Run smoke similarity checks on the small internal sample set (script: scripts/quick-sim-check.sh)
- [ ] Watch logs for N+ error patterns for 30m (esp. downstream batchers)
- [ ] If stable, close JIRA with rollback note and next steps for embed-v2 remediation plan

Escalation path (who to call if alarms):
- First: Priya Desai (pager)
- Second: Anil Kapoor (platform infra lead)
- Third: Product PM (Rowan Mitchell)

Metrics to watch (quick list):
- Similarity delta on short queries (internal metric: sim.short.delta) — primary
- 5xx rate on embedding endpoints (endpoint.errors.5xx) — secondary
- Median tail latency (p50/p95) for embeddings
- Customer error reports (CS slack thread + Zendesk tag)

Notes to self (things I want to capture after the event):
- Timestamp of routing change + console request ID
- Any correlation with recent quantization change (embedding-quantization v3 applied last week)
- Full diff of evaluation results for internal prompt suite (save to confluence under embed-v2-investigation)
- Who observed the regression first (link to Slack snippet)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want to re-run embed-v2 with stricter calibration on short queries? (action: schedule eval job with @applied-ml)
- Is there a safe canary ramp strategy (5% -> 15%) for reintroducing after fix?
- Should we create a small customer-facing note template in case CS needs to notify enterprise customers?

Slack snippets for quick copy-paste (internal watch):
- Internal ops short: "Rolling back embed-v2 canary (10%) to embed-v1 for stability. Monitoring for 60m. JIRA-5582. Ping #ops-embed-incident for customer reports."
- CS quick line: "We're performing a brief routing rollback to preserve embedding quality; no action needed from you unless you see regressions. CS will notify if an account is impacted."

Final reminders before I hit send:
- Keep language low-friction and non-alarming; avoid words like "outage" or "failure" if not true.
- Record all timestamps in the JIRA ticket (change start/complete).
- Preserve canary config (don’t delete embed-v2 variant) so we can reintroduce after fixes.

-- end of crib.

(Notes: this is a personal scratchpad — will copy into a tidy Slack post once Priya signs off. Save a snapshot of this note in the JIRA when closing.)
